instruction.text: What’s happening at the sandpit? Select the red bucket to find out.

feedback.end: Melina borrowed Casper’s bucket to play with. She doesn’t want to give it back because she is having so much fun building sandcastles.

instruction.text: What is the problem at the sandpit about? What would an agreement look like? Listen to the options and drag them to the correct group.

atoms.sound: Melina keeps Casper’s bucket for herself.
Melina agrees to return Casper’s things to him.

feedback.finish: Finding the problem right away can help solve the conflict. Solving the conflict as early as possible can avoid even bigger problems.

instruction.text: What would a bigger problem look like in Melina and Casper’s situation? What would an agreement look like? Listen to the options and drag them to the correct group.

hint.text: If there is a fight, there is a problem. Apologies usually show that there is an agreement.

atoms.sound: Melina and Casper are fighting over the bucket.
After a long talk, Melina apologises for keeping Casper’s bucket.

instruction.text: Listen to the dialogue between Casper and Melina to find out how talking about a problem can help.

atoms.b: This bucket makes the best sandcastles ever! I love the red colour too.
Yeah, I know... but I would like to have my bucket back now. You have been playing with it all day.
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-1st'>Yeah, I know... but I would like to have my bucket back now. You have been playing with it all day.</prosody>

atoms.b: But I’m having so much fun! And my sandcastles look much better than yours.
That’s not fair. How would you feel if I stole one of your toys?
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-1st'>That’s not fair. How would you feel if I stole one of your toys?</prosody>

atoms.b: Well... I don’t think I would like that. Wow, Casper. I’m so sorry. I did not realise how selfish I was being.
That’s okay. Just make sure not to do it again. You can always play with my bucket if we take turns!
